title: Cap. IX Arg. 4: God is ready to give all sufficient media to believe and convert — therefore reprobation only by consequent will after foresight of final impenitence
latin: Urgent adhuc fortius; Deus ipse ex parte sua paratus est dare omnibus media sufficientia et necessaria ad credendum et convertendum, ac dabit proculdubio nisi obicem ipsi posuerint: Videntur autem haec inter se pugnare, ut Deus voluntate antecedente aliquem reprobaverit, et tamen paratus sit ei suppeditare omnia ad salutem necessaria: Neminem ergo reprobavit nisi voluntate consequente praevisam ejusdem hominis finalem impoenitentiam, infidelitatem, gratiaeque Divinae rejectionem.
pass_a: They urge still more strongly; God himself on his part is prepared to give unto all media sufficient and necessary unto believing and converting, and will doubtless give them unless they themselves put an obstacle: But these things seem to fight among themselves, that God by antecedent will should have reprobated someone, and yet be prepared to supply unto him all things necessary unto salvation: Therefore he reprobated no one except by consequent will the foresighted final impenitence, unbelief, and rejection of Divine grace of the same man.
pass_b: They press harder still: God on his part is ready to give everyone the media sufficient and needful for believing and converting, and will surely give them unless people themselves put up a barrier. But that seems to clash — that God by antecedent will should have reprobated someone, and yet be ready to supply him everything needful for salvation. Therefore, they say, he reprobated no one except by consequent will after foresight of that person's final impenitence, unbelief, and rejection of divine grace.

lemmas.gloss: God ready to give all sufficient media to believe/convert
adversaries: reprobation only after foresight final impenitence

title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: universal sufficient grace is a slippery postulate — Vasquez grants some infants never received sufficient media of salvation
latin: Illud de gratia sufficiente omnibus parata et administrata postulatum valde lubricum est, et inter ipsos gratiae universalis patronos nondum pleno et firmo consensu approbatum. Vasques (quod ante annotavimus) ipsa rei evidentia convictus concedit, quibusdam infantibus sufficientia salutis media neque humana ulla providentia potuisse applicari, neque Divina providentia fuisse applicata, In T. Aquin. disp. 95. cap. 6. Possumus igitur, quoad hosce parvulos in originali peccato sic pereuntes, retorquere hanc rationem hoc modo: Quibus infantibus media sufficientia praeparata et administrata non fuerunt, illi rejecti fuerunt sine consideratione actualis infidelitatis, aut finalis impoenitentiae.
pass_a: That postulate concerning sufficient grace prepared and administered unto all is very slippery, and among the patrons of universal grace themselves has not yet been approved by full and firm consent. Vasquez (which we noted before), convicted by the very evidence of the thing, grants that unto certain infants the sufficient media of salvation could neither by any human providence have been applied, nor by Divine providence were applied, In T. Aquin. disp. 95. cap. 6. We can therefore, as to these little ones so perishing in original sin, turn back this reason thus: Those infants unto whom sufficient media were not prepared and administered were rejected without consideration of actual unbelief, or of final impenitence.
pass_b: The claim that sufficient grace is prepared and administered to all is very slippery — and even among patrons of universal grace it lacks full firm consent. Vasquez (as we noted before), forced by the plain fact, grants that for some infants sufficient media of salvation could not be applied by any human providence and were not applied by divine providence (In T. Aquin. disp. 95.6). So for these little ones perishing in original sin we can turn their argument back: infants for whom sufficient media were never prepared or administered were rejected without regard to actual unbelief or final impenitence.

lemmas.gloss: some infants never received sufficient media

title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: infants of unbelieving idolaters — rejection without foresight of the reprobate's unbelief; Vasquez also grants some adult reprobation before foresight of sins
latin: Sed quibusdam infantibus (puta ex utroque parente infideli idololatra, Christum nesciente, diabolum colente, susceptis, quos ἀκάθαρτοι ipse Apostolus indigitavit, 1 Cor. vii. 14.) sufficientia media non fuere praeparata aut administrata: In talibus ergo coguntur agnoscere rejectionem absque respectu ad praevisam et praeconsideratam personae reprobatae infidelitatem. Sed missis infantibus, qui Divina providentia ita ordinante nascuntur et moriuntur extra Ecclesiam, Idem Vasques et illud largitur, Et a praevisione peccatorum, etiam quoad adultos et rationis ac liberi arbitrii compotes, fuisse aliquam reprobationem et repulsam a Deo praefinitam, ibid. cap. 2. Reprobationem autem intelligit, rejectionem ab illa gratia speciali, qua negata homo semper indurescit et in perditionem ruit, cap. 5.
pass_a: But unto certain infants (for example those taken up from both parents an unbelieving idolater, not knowing Christ, worshipping the devil — whom the Apostle himself marked as unclean, 1 Cor. vii. 14.) sufficient media were not prepared or administered: In such therefore they are compelled to acknowledge rejection without respect unto the foresighted and preconsidered unbelief of the reprobated person. But setting aside infants who, Divine providence so ordaining, are born and die outside the Church, the same Vasquez also grants this, that even as to adults possessed of reason and free will, some reprobation and repulse was predetermined by God from before the foresight of sins, ibid. cap. 2. But by reprobation he understands rejection from that special grace which, being denied, a man always hardens and rushes into perdition, cap. 5.
pass_b: Take infants born of two unbelieving idolatrous parents — knowing no Christ, serving the devil — whom the Apostle himself calls unclean (1 Cor. 7:14): for them sufficient media were neither prepared nor administered. In such cases they must grant rejection with no regard to foresight of the reprobate's unbelief. Set those infants aside who, under divine providence, are born and die outside the Church: the same Vasquez also grants that even for adults with reason and free will some reprobation and repulse was fixed by God before foresight of sins (ibid. cap. 2). By reprobation he means rejection from that special grace which, denied, leaves a man always hardening and rushing into perdition (cap. 5).

lemmas.gloss: infants of idolaters without sufficient media
some adult reprobation before foresight of sins

title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: supply of sufficient grace does not exclude antecedent reprobation — preparation of efficacious grace does, and implies election
latin: Si Arminius, Corvinus, eorumque assipulatores vel hoc nobis concesserint, sequetur sufficientis gratiae suppeditationem non excludere antecedaneam reprobationem, sed efficacis gratiae praeparationem revera illam excludere, et electionem inferre. Sumatur igitur, omnibus adultis gratiam sufficientem a Deo administrari, tamen (uti videtis) vel Jesuita judice, non inde sequitur eos non fuisse ante praevisionem finalium demeritorum reprobatos.
pass_a: If Arminius, Corvinus, and their assenterers will grant us even this, it will follow that the supplying of sufficient grace does not exclude antecedent reprobation, but that the preparation of efficacious grace does in truth exclude it, and brings in election. Let it therefore be taken, that sufficient grace is administered by God unto all adults, yet (as you see) even with a Jesuit as judge, it does not thence follow that they were not reprobated before the foresight of final demerits.
pass_b: If Arminius, Corvinus, and their backers grant us even that much, it follows that supplying sufficient grace does not shut out antecedent reprobation — whereas preparing efficacious grace truly does shut it out, and brings election in. So grant that God administers sufficient grace to every adult: still (as you see), even by a Jesuit's judgment, it does not follow they were not reprobated before foresight of final demerits.

lemmas.gloss: sufficient grace compatible with antecedent reprobation
efficacious-grace prep excludes reprobation; implies election

title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: apostate angels received sufficient media yet some were elect, some reprobate — so sufficient grace to all would not prove reprobation only from foresight of final unbelief
latin: In Angelis apostatis hujus rei veritas liquido apparet. Deus non modo paratus fuit dare illis media sufficientia et necessaria ad standum et perseverandum in obsequio Divino, sed dedit: ac nihilominus omnes Theologi fatentur, inter ipsos Angelos quosdam fuisse electos, quosdam non-electos sive reprobatos. Si igitur adversarii possint evincere, omnibus et singulis hominibus gratiam sufficientem dari, non tamen idcirco recte intulerint, neminem nisi ex praevisione finalis infidelitatis reprobari. Nam sicuti posita gratia sufficiente quoad designatam aliquam personam, non ponitur idcirco antecedanea ejus praedestinatio; ita nec posita eadem gratia sufficiente quoad eandem personam negatur idcirco antecedanea ejusdem reprobatio.
pass_a: In the apostate Angels the truth of this matter appears clearly. God was not only prepared to give unto them media sufficient and necessary unto standing and persevering in Divine obedience, but he gave them: and nevertheless all Theologians confess that among the Angels themselves some were elect, some non-elect or reprobate. If therefore the adversaries could prove that sufficient grace is given unto all and singular men, they would not therefore rightly infer that no one is reprobated except from foresight of final unbelief. For as, sufficient grace being posited as to some designated person, his antecedent predestination is not therefore posited; so neither, the same sufficient grace being posited as to the same person, is his antecedent reprobation therefore denied.
pass_b: The apostate angels make this plain. God was not only ready to give them media sufficient and needful to stand and persevere in divine obedience — he gave them. Yet every theologian grants that among the angels some were elect, some non-elect or reprobate. So even if the adversaries could prove sufficient grace is given to every human being, they still could not rightly infer that no one is reprobated except from foresight of final unbelief. Just as positing sufficient grace for a given person does not posit his antecedent predestination, so positing that same sufficient grace does not deny his antecedent reprobation.

lemmas.gloss: angels got sufficient media; some elect, some reprobate
sufficient grace neither proves election nor denies reprobation

title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: predestination is ordination with infallible event; reprobation denies unfrustrable special operation — Bellarmine: God not bound to give sufficient grace to all
latin: Ratio utrobique eadem est; Quia praedestinatio non dicit quamlibet ordinationem ad finem supernaturalem per media quantovis sufficientia, sed ordinationem cum exitu et eventu infallibili copulatam; neque reprobatio negat omnem ordinationem ad finem supernaturalem, sed ordinationem infrustrabilem ex inventione et speciali operatione Dei ordinantis, ipsum salutis eventum producentem. Denique, sufficientia media ad salutem omnibus dari, non tanta facilitate probatur quanta confidentia affirmatur. Non jam ingrediar hanc disputationem, quia ad solutionem argumenti propositi (uti accepistis) non est necesse. Illud solummodo annotabo, Bellarminum, qui hanc de sufficiente gratia sententiam tuetur, primo concedere nobis, quod nulla esset in Deo iniquitas si negaret aliquibus vel omnibus hanc gratiam sufficientem, De grat. et lib. arb. l. 2. cap. 4. Hinc colligimus, Deum nullo pacto aut promissione ad hoc obligatum: Quomodo igitur adversarii audent promittere omnibus et singulis gratiam sufficientem, quam Deus non promisit?
pass_a: The reason on both sides is the same; Because predestination does not mean any ordination whatsoever unto a supernatural end through media however sufficient, but an ordination coupled with an infallible issue and event; nor does reprobation deny every ordination unto a supernatural end, but an unfrustrable ordination from the device and special operation of the ordaining God, producing the very event of salvation. Finally, that sufficient media unto salvation are given unto all is not proved with as much facility as it is affirmed with confidence. I will not now enter this dispute, because for the solution of the argument proposed (as you have received) it is not necessary. This only I will note, that Bellarmine, who defends this opinion concerning sufficient grace, first grants us that there would be no iniquity in God if he denied this sufficient grace unto some or unto all, De grat. et lib. arb. l. 2. cap. 4. Hence we gather that God is bound unto this by no pact or promise: How then do the adversaries dare to promise unto all and singular sufficient grace, which God has not promised?
pass_b: The reason is the same either way. Predestination is not just any ordination to a supernatural end by media however sufficient — it is ordination joined to an infallible outcome. Reprobation does not deny every ordination to a supernatural end, but the unfrustrable ordination that comes from the ordaining God's device and special operation producing the very event of salvation. Finally: that sufficient media of salvation are given to all is asserted with more confidence than it is proved with ease. I will not enter that dispute now — it is not needed to solve the argument before us. One note only: Bellarmine, who defends this sufficient-grace view, first grants that God would do no injustice if he denied that sufficient grace to some or to all (De grat. et lib. arb. 2.4). So God is bound to it by no pact or promise. How then dare the adversaries promise every person sufficient grace that God never promised?

lemmas.gloss: God not bound to give sufficient grace; adversaries over-promise
